output.summary: Perennial nettle found in Japan, China and Taiwan, where it inhabits moist mountain forests. Its stinging hairs can cause pain, redness, burning or itching. After boiling to destroy its toxicity, it is used in Taiwan in soup, bread, shortbread and fried leaves.
output.edibilityNote: Boiling destroys its toxicity; Taiwanese uses include soup, bread, Chinese shortbread and crispy fried leaves.
